intro: Copy files from a computer, phone or USB drive.
prerequisite: FTP and these file managers need an already compatible homebrew setup. Check your exact console firmware first. A normal retail console does not provide this FTP access.
sameNetwork: For FTP, connect both devices to the same local network. Keep the console awake and its FTP service running. A wired console connection can help with large files.
ps4Setup: With your compatible GoldHEN setup active, open GoldHEN settings, open Server Settings and enable the FTP server. GoldHEN normally uses port 2121. If you use another server, use its displayed port and login details.
ps5Setup: Start a PS5 FTP server supported by your firmware and loader. The ftpsrv payload normally uses port 2121. etaHEN has a separate optional FTP service on port 1337; enable it in your installed build’s settings or configuration. Use the port of the service you actually started.
ipStep: Write down the console’s IPv4 address and FTP port. Use the console address, not your phone’s address or your router’s address. The address in the picture is only an example.
networkCaption: 1: same local network. 2: console with FTP running. 3: console IP and port. 4: connecting device.
plainFtp: FTP · plain FTP when encryption is unsupported
loginValue: Use the login details required by your running FTP server.
localOnly: Plain FTP is unencrypted. Use your own trusted local network and turn the server off when you finish. Do not forward the FTP port on your router.
clientNote: Install FileZilla Client on Windows, macOS or Linux. The console runs the FTP server.
fz1: Open File → Site Manager → New site. Choose FTP. Enter your console IP and port. If the server has no TLS support, choose Only use plain FTP. For servers with anonymous access, choose Anonymous; otherwise use the login required by your server. Select Connect.
fz2: The left pane is your computer. The right pane is your console. On the left, find your completed download. On the right, open the folder required by that file’s installation guide. For a simple transfer test, use a new folder inside /data.
fz3: Drag the file from the left pane to the right pane, or right-click it and choose Upload. To copy a file back to your computer, use Download on the console side. If a file already exists, skip it or choose a new name until you have checked it.
fz4: Wait for the queue to finish. Check Failed transfers, then refresh the destination and compare the filename and size. Keep your original copy. If the connection drops, check the partial file before resuming or retrying.
fzCaption: 1: connection settings. 2: your computer. 3: your console. 4: transfer queue. Upload goes from 2 to 3.
phoneIntro: Download the file to your phone first. Then open an FTP client and upload it to the console. An FTP server app on your phone is a different tool.
iosSteps: In FTPManager, add an FTP connection using the console IP, port and server login. Allow Local Network access if iOS asks. Open the completed download in Files and use Share to copy it into FTPManager if needed. In the app, copy or upload the local file to the console folder.
androidSteps: In Solid Explorer, add a storage connection and choose FTP. Enter the console IP, port and server login. Open Downloads, select the completed file and choose Copy. Open the console connection, enter the destination folder and choose Paste. Allow access to the local file when asked.
harmonySteps: electerm has a native HarmonyOS app with FTP support. Add an FTP connection, enter the console IP, port and server login, then upload a local file to the destination. App availability and controls can vary by region and release.
harmonyNote: HarmonyOS NEXT needs a native compatible app. Older Huawei phones that support Android apps may use a compatible Android FTP client. Check your device and store listing before installing; an Android APK is not a native HarmonyOS NEXT app.
phoneFinish: Keep the FTP app open until the upload finishes. Refresh the console folder and compare the file size. If the app cannot see the download, import it from Files or Downloads and retry.
phoneCaption: 1: saved file. 2: FTP connection. 3: console folder. 4: uploaded copy. These are example screens, not exact app menus.
usb1: Use a drive readable by your file manager. exFAT is usually the practical choice for large files; FAT32 has a single-file limit of just under 4 GiB. Formatting erases the drive, so copy anything you need elsewhere first. A drive formatted as PlayStation extended storage is not an ordinary transfer drive.
usb2: On your computer or compatible phone with a USB adapter, copy the file into a clearly named folder on the USB drive. Wait for copying to finish, safely eject it, then connect it to the console.
usb3: Open your console file manager and look under /mnt for the mounted USB drive. Names such as /mnt/usb0 and /mnt/usb1 are examples, not fixed USB socket numbers. Find your folder and check the filename.
usb4: Select the file or folder, choose Copy, open the required internal destination and choose Paste. Wait for completion and compare the file size. Keep the USB original until you have checked the copy. Copying a file does not install or run it.
usbCaption: 1: original file on USB. 2: actual USB mount. 3: required destination. 4: copied file.
ps4ManagerIntro: Use the existing PS4-Xplorer 2.07 listing for PS4. Install its PS4 PKG with your compatible package installer, then start PS4-Xplorer from the console home screen.
ps4ManagerSteps: Browse to the source file, open the app’s action menu and choose Copy. Browse to the destination and choose Paste. Use New folder when you need a separate destination. Read the control hints in your installed version; button mappings and modes can differ.
ps5ManagerIntro: Use ezRemote Client 2.18 for PS5. Extract its app files into /data/homebrew as the release describes. Start the included ezRemote-Loader-1.01.elf through your compatible Payload Manager / elfldr setup. This loader does not need websrv. This is a different app from PS4-Xplorer.
ps5ManagerSteps: Open the PS5 client, browse local storage or the mounted USB drive, select your file and choose Copy. Open the destination and choose Paste. Follow the control hints shown by the installed client. Package installation is a separate action; check the release’s package and firmware requirements first.
managerFinish: Use Copy for your first transfer. Back up an existing destination before replacing anything. Do not change system folders or permissions unless the file’s own instructions require it. Saved games need the matching save-management tool.
destinationNote: There is no single destination for every download. A plugin, save, package and payload each have their own setup. Follow the exact platform, firmware, game update and folder instructions on the download’s page.
pkgNote: A PKG must still be installed with a compatible installer. A ZIP must be extracted when the instructions say so. A BIN or ELF needs its matching loader. Renaming a file does not convert it.
helpConnect: Cannot connect? Check the console IP, same network, active FTP service and its exact port. Guest Wi-Fi, VPNs and router device isolation can block local connections. Allow the FTP client through your computer firewall.
helpLogin: Login or encryption error? Check the server’s authentication and TLS support. Do not use SFTP for an FTP-only server. A web file manager on port 8080 is not the FTP service.
helpLarge: A large file fails on USB? Check free space and the drive format. FAT32 cannot hold a file of 4 GiB or larger. On FTP, inspect failed transfers and keep the console awake.
helpFolder: Cannot see the file? Refresh the folder, check the actual USB mount and confirm the download finished. A downloaded HTML error page is not the intended file.
centerIntro: The Download Center is still being organised. The existing PS4 and PS5 downloads and the guides below are available now.
centerNote: Choose your console before downloading. Keep the listed firmware and game compatibility requirements.
phoneSaving: Help saving files on a phone
reviewed: Guide reviewed 11 November 2026. Transfers on physical consoles have not been tested here.
pictureAlt: Numbered transfer diagram with highlighted connection fields, devices and file paths
ps4Summary: Simple PS4 FileZilla, iPhone, Android, HarmonyOS FTP and USB instructions, with screenshots and PS4-Xplorer file management.
ps5Summary: Simple PS5 FileZilla, iPhone, Android, HarmonyOS FTP and USB instructions, with screenshots and ezRemote Client file management.
methodQuestion: How do you want to transfer files?
ftpHint: Use your local network. No USB drive needed.
usbHint: Use a USB drive and the console file manager.
ipCaption: Follow the highlighted menu items. Copy the address shown on your own console; 192.168.1.50 is an example.
goldhenCaption: With compatible GoldHEN already active, open Server Settings and enable FTP. Keep the console awake while copying.
guideCardIntro: Choose FTP or USB for a simple guide with pictures, phone apps and file management steps.
deviceQuestion: What will you use for FTP?
managerCaption: 1: select the source file. 2: choose Copy. 3: open the destination. 4: choose Paste and wait for completion.
ps5ToolSummary: Manage PS5 files with ezRemote Client 2.18. Start the included loader 1.01 through a compatible elfldr setup; this release’s loader no longer needs websrv.
ps4Controls: In PS4-Xplorer, Cross opens or confirms, Circle goes back, and Triangle opens the action menu for Copy or Paste. Follow the hints in your installed version if its controls differ.
ps5Controls: In PS5 ezRemote, Cross opens an item, Square marks files, Triangle opens Actions, and L2 opens the parent folder. USB-to-internal copying stays in the local file list. Options exits the app.
iosConnect: Tap + and choose FTP. Enter your console’s IP address, FTP port and server login. Save and open the connection. Allow Local Network access if iOS asks.
iosFind: Find the completed download in Files. If it is outside FTPManager, use Share to open it in the app. In FTPManager, open Local, select the file and choose Copy to.
iosUpload: Choose your saved console connection and open the destination folder. Confirm the copy. When it finishes, refresh the console folder and compare the file size.
androidConnect: Open the side menu in Solid Explorer and go to Storage manager. Tap +, choose FTP and enter your console’s IP address, FTP port and server login. Finish the wizard and open the connection.
androidFind: Open Downloads in Solid Explorer. Touch and hold the completed file, then tap Copy. Open your saved FTP connection and browse to the destination folder.
androidUpload: Tap Paste. Wait for the copy to finish, then refresh the console folder and compare the file size.
harmonyConnect: In electerm, open Bookmarks and add a new connection. Select FTP, enter your console’s IP address, FTP port and server login, then save and open the connection.
harmonyFind: In the connection’s file browser, open the console folder required by your download. Choose Upload and select the completed file from your phone.
harmonyUpload: Keep electerm open while it uploads. When the copy finishes, refresh the console folder and compare the file size.
